lines.text: [excited] Imagine being so weak that nobody even takes you seriously as a hunter. Now imagine finding out that one simple glass of tea can make someone strong enough to beat monsters they never could before.
And the craziest part? The guy selling that tea isn't some legendary warrior or a powerful mage. He's an eighteen-year-old kid running a tiny tea stall.
This is The F-Rank Tea Seller, our very own webtoon, where one glass of chai might be worth more than a whole room full of weapons.
Now, this episode actually opens at the end, with Viktor glowing and shouting, where is this power coming from? Then it jumps back one hour, to show us how he got there.

[mysterious] So, Mumbai, in the year twenty thirty-one. But this isn't the Mumbai we know today. Mysterious Gates have opened all over the world, and behind every Gate there's a dungeon full of monsters.

The people who can fight those monsters are called Hunters. They go in, kill whatever's inside, and bring back monster cores, which sell for serious money. For a strong Hunter, this new world is basically a gold mine.
But not everyone gets a share of that gold. Right next to the biggest Gate in the city, there's a tiny tea stall, and behind the counter is a young man named Arjun.
[funny] Arjun's eighteen, and technically, he is a Hunter. His rank is F... the weakest rank there is. In a world where your rank decides your value, he's right at the bottom of the food chain.
So instead of fighting monsters, he sells chai, ten rupees a glass. And judging by how quiet the street is, even that isn't making him rich.
Things get interesting when a group of professional Hunters walks up to the stall. Leading them is Viktor Hale, a B-Rank Hunter with two million followers.
[funny] He's strong, he's famous, and he knows it. Sadly, his manners are nowhere near as impressive as his follower count. Every office has one Viktor, right? The loudest one in every meeting.
The moment Viktor spots Arjun, he turns it into a show. To him, an F-Rank has no business standing anywhere near a Gate, let alone selling something to real Hunters.
But Arjun doesn't lose his temper. He just offers him a glass, and says it's good for the nerves before a dungeon. Which is a very polite way of saying... you look nervous.

[funny] Of course, Viktor takes that as another chance to make fun of him. Tea from an F-Rank? He actually asks if it's poisoned with weakness. He's already decided Arjun is useless, without giving him a single chance.
[warm] Luckily, not everyone in the group thinks like Viktor. Meera, their healer, tells him to be nice and buys three teas. She's the only one in the party who treats Arjun like a person.
Viktor drinks his in one gulp and says it's nothing special. As far as he's concerned, it's just an ordinary cup of chai.
[mysterious] Then, as they walk toward the Gate, Arjun wishes them luck... and says something that sounds completely unimportant. One hour. That's all you get.
Keep that number in your head, because it's the most important thing anyone says in this whole episode.
[serious] The team walks into a level nine dungeon, expecting a normal day at work. It doesn't stay normal for very long.
The monsters inside are way stronger than they should be. Ogres, monster wolves, all of them hitting much harder than anything in a level nine dungeon ever should.
Their tank, the guy whose whole job is to take the hits, gets thrown across the cave. That's when you know it's bad.
Viktor's struggling too. He's a B-Rank, this place should be easy for him, and he honestly can't understand why these ogres are this strong.
Meera's already telling everyone to retreat. For the first time, the famous Hunter is in a fight where confidence just isn't enough.
[shocked] And right when it looks hopeless, something strange happens. Viktor feels a huge surge of power, and golden light starts pouring out of his body.
[excited] One swing... and the ogre that was beating him a minute ago is just gone.
His own team can't believe it. Where did that come from? He hasn't learned a new skill, nobody handed him a magic sword, and nothing in that dungeon should make him this strong.
[funny] So Viktor comes up with the only explanation that makes sense to Viktor. He has awakened. Of course he has. He's just that special.
And honestly, who could blame him? If you went from losing to an ogre to one-shotting it, you'd think something amazing happened to you too.
But we know something he doesn't. Before he walked in, Viktor drank a cheap glass of tea... from the guy he called useless.
For the next fifty-eight minutes, he's unstoppable. He goes through that dungeon like it's a tutorial level. And if you've been counting the minutes... you can probably guess where this is going.
[serious] Then they reach the boss. A giant minotaur in black armor, with an axe bigger than a car. The kind of monster a B-Rank should never fight alone.
Viktor doesn't even think. He jumps in for the final hit, full of confidence... and that's exactly when the clock reaches sixty minutes.
[funny] The golden light just fizzles out, right there in the air. And Viktor's face says everything. Oh no.
[funny] So the great Viktor Hale, two million followers, does the smartest thing he does all day. He runs. Just like the office Viktor... first one out the door when the real work starts.
They crawl out of the Gate barely alive. Whatever happened in there, it was much more dangerous than anyone expected.
[shocked] Viktor goes straight to the tea stall, grabs Arjun, and demands to know what he put in that tea.
Think about that for a second. This morning, Arjun was a nobody. Now the famous Hunter is standing in front of him, begging for answers. The irony is almost too good.
[funny] And Arjun, totally calm, gives him the most honest answer possible... cardamom.
[funny] Ask any mother why her chai tastes better than yours, and you'll get the exact same answer. Cardamom.

[funny] Meanwhile, Meera has clearly figured something out. She just holds up her coins and asks if she can get one to go. Smartest person in the whole episode. And remember that glass, because it's going to matter.
[mysterious] That night, when the street is empty, the story finally shows us what's really going on.
Arjun has a hidden skill called Hunter's Chai. Its rank is unknown, and what it does is simple. Anyone who drinks his tea borrows a huge amount of strength... for exactly one hour.
So suddenly, everything in that dungeon makes sense. Viktor didn't awaken. He was running on borrowed power, and the moment that hour ran out, he was back to being plain old Viktor.
[funny] And what's Arjun's big thought about all this? Ten rupees for an hour of power... he's undercharging. My office canteen charges more than that for a cold samosa.

But think about what this really means. Arjun doesn't need to be the strongest fighter in the world. He doesn't even need to walk into a dungeon. He can make any Hunter stronger, just by handing them a glass of chai.
That little roadside stall might be the most valuable place in all of Mumbai, and nobody knows it yet.
[mysterious] But there's one more thing. Deep inside the Gate, something huge opens one glowing red eye... and it looks like it noticed.
If the Hunters barely survived a level nine dungeon, whatever's watching from in there is on a completely different level. And Arjun is sitting on a secret that could change the whole Hunter world.

[warm] Ten rupees a glass. One hour of borrowed power. And a mystery that's only just started. You can read episode one free on WEBTOON, just search The F-Rank Tea Seller. So tell me in the comments... what would you do with one hour of power?
